quests.hint: Noun for the feeling of looking forward to something. There was a lot of ____ before the movie's release date.
quests.explanation: ANTICIPATE + -ION = ANTICIPATION. Dropping the silent E of ANTICIPATE before -ION forms a noun naming the excitement of expecting something.

quests.hint: Adjective describing something people were expecting or looking forward to. The ____ sequel finally hit theaters this weekend.
quests.explanation: ANTICIPATE + -D = ANTICIPATED. Adding -D to ANTICIPATE forms an adjective describing something that was expected in advance.

quests.hint: Adjective describing something that came as a surprise, not expected in advance. The ____ traffic made everyone late for the meeting.
quests.explanation: UN- + ANTICIPATED = UNANTICIPATED. This reviews the UN- prefix once again, attached here to the past-tense ANTICIPATED to mean 'not expected'.

quests.hint: Noun for a careful judgment of the quality or value of something. The teacher's ____ of the essay included detailed feedback.
quests.explanation: EVALUATE + -ION = EVALUATION. Dropping the silent E of EVALUATE before -ION forms a noun naming the process of judging something's value.

quests.hint: Adjective describing something designed to judge quality or performance. The course ends with an ____ project instead of a written exam.
quests.explanation: EVALUATE + -IVE = EVALUATIVE. Built on the same base as EVALUATION, -IVE here forms an adjective describing something used for judging.

quests.hint: Noun for a person whose job is to judge the quality or value of something. An outside ____ reviewed the school's new curriculum.
quests.explanation: EVALUATE + -OR = EVALUATOR. Dropping the silent E before -OR names the person who performs the evaluation.

quests.hint: Noun for the act of making a process easier for others. Her ____ of the discussion kept the meeting on schedule.
quests.explanation: FACILITATE + -ION = FACILITATION. Dropping the silent E of FACILITATE before -ION forms a noun naming the act of helping a process run smoothly.

quests.hint: Noun for a person who helps a group work through a discussion or process. The workshop ____ kept everyone focused on the goal.
quests.explanation: FACILITATE + -OR = FACILITATOR. Dropping the silent E before -OR names the person who guides a group process without dominating it.

quests.hint: Adjective describing an approach that helps a process along rather than controls it. The manager took a ____ role instead of giving direct orders.
quests.explanation: FACILITATE + -IVE = FACILITATIVE. Built on the same base as FACILITATOR, -IVE here forms an adjective describing a supportive, guiding style.

quests.hint: Noun for the process of putting a plan or decision into action. The ____ of the new policy will begin next month.
quests.explanation: IMPLEMENT + -ATION = IMPLEMENTATION. Adding -ATION to the verb IMPLEMENT forms a noun naming the process of carrying out a plan.

quests.hint: Adjective describing a plan that is realistic enough to actually carry out. The committee looked for a solution that was both fair and ____.
quests.explanation: IMPLEMENT + -ABLE = IMPLEMENTABLE. Adding -ABLE to IMPLEMENT forms an adjective describing a plan that can practically be put into action.

quests.hint: Adjective describing a plan or idea that was never put into action. The budget cuts left several ____ proposals sitting on the shelf.
quests.explanation: UN- + IMPLEMENTED = UNIMPLEMENTED. This reviews the UN- prefix, here attached to the past-tense IMPLEMENTED to mean 'never carried out'.

quests.hint: Adjective describing an amount large enough to matter. There was a ____ difference between the two job offers' salaries.
quests.explanation: SUBSTANCE + -TIAL = SUBSTANTIAL. The ending -CE of SUBSTANCE changes to -T before -IAL: SUBSTANCE becomes SUBSTANT, then + IAL = SUBSTANTIAL.

quests.hint: Adverb describing a change large enough to matter. Ticket prices increased ____ after the venue was renovated.
quests.explanation: SUBSTANTIAL + -LY = SUBSTANTIALLY. Adding -LY to the adjective SUBSTANTIAL forms the adverb, describing the size of a change or difference.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to provide evidence that proves something is true. The reporter couldn't ____ the rumor with any real facts.
quests.explanation: SUBSTANCE + -TIATE = SUBSTANTIATE. Unlike SUBSTANTIAL, which describes size, SUBSTANTIATE is a verb meaning to back up a claim with solid proof.

quests.hint: Noun for the act of removing something completely. The new filter allows for the ____ of almost all bacteria in the water.
quests.explanation: ELIMINATE + -ION = ELIMINATION. Dropping the silent E of ELIMINATE before -ION forms a noun naming the act of getting rid of something entirely.

quests.hint: Verb meaning to treat one task as more important and handle it first. When the schedule gets tight, she has to ____ the urgent tasks.
quests.explanation: PRIORITY + -IZE = PRIORITIZE. Dropping the final Y of PRIORITY before -IZE forms a verb meaning 'to rank in order of importance'.

quests.hint: Noun for the process of deciding what is most important. The team's ____ of tasks helped them hit the deadline.
quests.explanation: PRIORITIZE + -ATION = PRIORITIZATION. Adding -ATION to the verb PRIORITIZE forms a noun naming the process of ranking things by importance.

quests.hint: Noun for the organized effort to make different parts work together smoothly. Good ____ between departments kept the event running on time.
quests.explanation: COORDINATE + -ION = COORDINATION. Dropping the silent E of COORDINATE before -ION forms a noun naming the smooth organization of different parts.

quests.hint: Noun for a person who organizes different parts of an event or project. The wedding ____ handled every vendor and deadline.
quests.explanation: COORDINATE + -OR = COORDINATOR. Dropping the silent E before -OR names the person who manages the moving parts of a plan.

quests.hint: Adjective describing a group that works together smoothly and effectively. It was clear from the first play that the team was well ____.
quests.explanation: COORDINATE + -D = COORDINATED. Adding -D to COORDINATE forms an adjective describing effective teamwork, completing the family with COORDINATION and COORDINATOR.

quests.hint: Noun for money or something else given to make up for a loss or inconvenience. Passengers received ____ for the canceled flight.
quests.explanation: COMPENSATE + -ION = COMPENSATION. Dropping the silent E of COMPENSATE before -ION forms a noun naming the payment or benefit given to balance out a loss.

quests.hint: Adjective describing something given to make up for a loss or unfair situation. Workers received ____ time off after the busy holiday season.
quests.explanation: COMPENSATE + -ORY = COMPENSATORY. Built on the same base as COMPENSATION, -ORY here forms an adjective describing something meant to balance out a loss.

quests.hint: Adjective describing extra work or effort that was never paid or rewarded. Volunteers put in hours of ____ overtime during the festival.
quests.explanation: UN- + COMPENSATED = UNCOMPENSATED. This reviews the UN- prefix, here attached to the past-tense COMPENSATED to mean 'not paid for'.

quests.hint: Noun for the act of recognizing or creating a difference between things. The report focused on the ____ between the two treatment groups.
quests.explanation: DIFFERENTIATE + -ION = DIFFERENTIATION. Dropping the silent E of DIFFERENTIATE before -ION forms a noun naming the act of telling things apart, built on the DIFFER family from much earlier.

quests.hint: Adjective describing a product or service designed to stand out from competitors. The brand's ____ packaging helped it stand out on crowded shelves.
quests.explanation: DIFFERENTIATE + -D = DIFFERENTIATED. Adding -D to DIFFERENTIATE forms an adjective describing something made noticeably distinct from similar things.

quests.hint: Adjective describing someone who shows no interest or preference either way. He seemed completely ____ about which restaurant they picked.
quests.explanation: IN- + DIFFERENT = INDIFFERENT. Watch out for this one: INDIFFERENT does not mean 'not different'. It means 'not caring', showing no interest either way.

quests.hint: Noun for a claim that makes something sound bigger or more dramatic than it really is. The ad was pulled after critics pointed out the ____.
quests.explanation: EXAGGERATE + -ION = EXAGGERATION. Dropping the silent E of EXAGGERATE before -ION forms a noun naming a claim that overstates the truth.

quests.hint: Adjective describing something made to sound bigger or more dramatic than reality. His ____ story about catching the fish got taller with every telling.
quests.explanation: EXAGGERATE + -D = EXAGGERATED. Adding -D to EXAGGERATE forms an adjective describing a claim or description that overstates the truth.

quests.hint: Adverb describing an action performed in an overstated, dramatic way. He ____ gasped when he saw the small spider on the wall.
quests.explanation: EXAGGERATED + -LY = EXAGGERATEDLY. Adding -LY to the adjective EXAGGERATED completes this family, closing out the higher-level vocabulary you've built through this stretch of levels.
